kizunaNote: The pull response carries changed rows, tombstones, a new cursor, and typed signals (P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints). D-conflict-journal-visibility makes conflicts optional, omitted when empty; C-2 fixes the key order when present: conflicts, cursor, has_more, rows, signal, tombstones.

items.kizunaNote: Selected D-conflict-journal-visibility shape for one overwritten column. winner_seq is the changelog seq of the winning write, always one of the seqs in the delivered page; pk must already be present in rows.

winner_seq.kizunaNote: The changelog seq of the write that won the column, which is what the item is joined by (D-conflict-journal-visibility). Same decimal-string seq the delivered rows[] entry carries, so a consumer matches them without a cast.

conflicts.kizunaNote: Optional D-conflict-journal-visibility contract, omitted when empty. conflict/004 pins the bytes; the SQL pack emits it and both clients persist _kizunasync_overwrites / COLUMN_OVERWRITTEN.

cursor.kizunaNote: The new cursor is a normative component (P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints); the client persists it only after durable apply. D-cursor-opaque-token ratified the opaque text encoding.

has_more.kizunaNote: D-page-cap-and-checkpoint-boundary and D-page-cap-and-checkpoint-boundary ratified has_more as the continuation marker: false closes the pull sequence and marks the boundary where the client atomically commits staged pages with the cursor (P:session-guarantees-and-exactly-once-effect item 2, P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints).

rows.kizunaNote: (seq, table, pk)-ordered (P:keyset-pagination-and-delivery-bound; invariant I-10). Latest state only: no row-image oplog (P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints).

signal.kizunaNote: D-signal-excludes-page-data ratified the exclusive signal shape enforced by invariant I-8: a non-null signal means empty rows and tombstones with has_more false.

tombstones.kizunaNote: Tombstones since cursor (P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints); same (seq, table, pk) ordering rule (invariant I-10).
